fieldValues.title: A capability a client needs before the core has it ships as a marked, tracked client stopgap that the core service replaces
fieldValues.decision_question: When a client needs a semantic capability that capability layering puts in the srs-repository core, but the core service does not exist yet, what does the client ship meanwhile?
fieldValues.context: srs-web#607 adds src/lib/record-duplication.ts; the muDemocracy site editor imports it (muDemocracy.org#378/#379), and muDemocracy.org#391 cannot point SRS_WEB_SHA at srs-web main until it merges. Capability layering (srs-rust/docs/architecture/capability-layering.md) puts such a capability once in the srs-repository core. Options put on #607: (a) file a core record duplicate service and close #607; (b) keep the TS helper in $lib as a stopgap and move the site editor onto it; (c) do nothing. Answers: SP-05 Case that prompted it: record duplication, srs-web#607 (merged 2026-10-28 as the stopgap) and the core service srs-rust#1505; muDemocracy.org#379 had a second copy in the site editor.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
1. Core first: build the core service and make clients wait. Leads to: no client copy ever exists, but client work is held up behind a core release.
2. Tracked stopgap (chosen): ship it in the client, marked temporary, with the core service filed. Leads to: clients move now; one client copy lives until the binding ships, and the paired issue keeps it from being forgotten.
3. Permanent client home: keep the capability in the client library. Leads to: fastest, but semantics live outside the core, against capability layering.
4. Do nothing: each client implements it where needed. Leads to: duplicated semantics across clients, as happened with record duplication.
fieldValues.key_requirements: Unblock muDemocracy.org#391 now; one lasting implementation in the core per capability layering; the stopgap is marked temporary and removed when the binding ships.
fieldValues.decision_statement: The client may ship the capability as a stopgap in its shared library, marked temporary in the code and paired with an issue for the core service (CLI and WASM). When the core binding ships, the stopgap is deleted and every client calls the binding. The stopgap is never the capability's permanent home.
fieldValues.rationale: It unblocks the site editor's move onto srs-web main today while keeping the layering rule: the client copy is time-boxed to the core service's arrival.
fieldValues.revisit_when: When a stopgap outlives its core binding by a release, or a second client copies a stopgap instead of calling it.
fieldValues.next_steps: Owner merges srs-web#607 (gate:owner-merge); muDemocracy.org#391 bumps SRS_WEB_SHA to the merge commit and drops the bindings override; srs-rust#1505 builds the core service.
